title: Sampling Colorings Close to the Maximum Degree: Non-Markovian Coupling and Local Uniformity
summary: Sampling graph colorings via local Markov chains is a central problem in approximate counting and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). We address the problem of sampling a random $k$-coloring of a graph with maximum degree $Δ$. The simplest algorithmic approach is to establish rapid mixing of the single-site update chain known as the Metropolis Glauber dynamics, which at each step chooses a random vertex $v$ and proposes a random color $c$, recoloring $v$ to $c$ if the resulting coloring remains proper. It is a long-standing open problem to prove that the Glauber dynamics has polynomial mixing…
